headline: Ukraine attack brings down part of the Crimean Bridge

chunks.text: On November 17, 2026, a Ukrainian attack {{brought down}} part of the bridge between Russia and Crimea. A [[steel arch]] and a section of road fell into the sea. Russia took the region of Crimea from Ukraine in 2014. That year, the United Nations asked all countries not to [[recognize]] the change. Russia later built the bridge. Ukraine's military said the damage {{cut off}} the [[road link]] and no [[vehicle]] could {{get across}}. Russia said trains ran again that day.

verbs.wrong: To mark a target on a map
verbs.why: Strong winds bring down old trees every winter. Workers bring down empty buildings with heavy machines. A Ukrainian attack brought down part of the bridge between Russia and Crimea.

verbs.correct: To stop a connection to a place
verbs.wrong: To make a road much wider
verbs.why: Heavy snow often cuts off mountain towns. Floods cut off small villages every spring. Ukraine's military said the damage cut off the road link to Crimea.
Small boats help people get across the lake. Most buses get across the river on the old bridge. Ukraine's military said no vehicle could get across after the attack.

chunks.text: Ukraine's President Zelenskyy called the attack [[unprecedented]], meaning never seen before. He said Ukrainian forces spent weeks {{wearing down}} Russian [[air defenses]] and {{knocked out}} [[radars]] before the [[final strike]]. Ukraine {{went after}} the bridge in 2022 and 2023. The bridge was damaged but {{held up}} both times. Zelenskyy said Ukraine was {{hitting back}} after Russian attacks on Ukrainian bridges, cities and [[energy systems]].

verbs.correct: To make something weaker over time
verbs.wrong: To sell weapons to an enemy
verbs.why: Constant stress wears down the body. Rough roads wear down car tires quickly. Zelenskyy said Ukrainian forces spent weeks wearing down Russian air defenses.

verbs.correct: To destroy or stop from working
verbs.wrong: To give something a new name
verbs.why: Storms often knock out power in our town. Lightning sometimes knocks out phone service here. Zelenskyy said his forces knocked out radars before the final strike.

verbs.correct: To try to attack a target
verbs.wrong: To sell a place to a bank
verbs.why: Hackers often go after small banks. Wolves go after the weakest animals in a group. Ukraine went after the bridge in 2022 and 2023.

verbs.wrong: To be moved to a new place
verbs.why: This old roof holds up in every storm. Cheap tents do not hold up in strong wind. The bridge was damaged in 2022 and 2023 but held up both times.

verbs.correct: To attack someone who attacked you
verbs.wrong: To forget an old enemy's name
verbs.why: A good boxer hits back after every punch. Some animals hit back when something attacks them. Zelenskyy said Ukraine was hitting back after repeated Russian attacks.

chunks.text: Russia's investigators opened a [[criminal case]] on [[terrorism charges]]. The Kremlin, the office of Russia's president, said the bridge would be [[restored]]. An engineering expert said crews could {{clean up}} the [[wreckage]] fairly quickly, but full road traffic would not return for more than a year. The Kremlin did not {{rule out}} a link between the attack and President Putin's trip to China. The attack came in the days {{leading up to}} his [[planned meeting]] with Presidents Trump and Xi.

verbs.why: Volunteers clean up the beach after big storms. Crews clean up broken glass after a car crash. An engineering expert said crews could clean up the wreckage fairly quickly.

verbs.correct: To say something is not possible
verbs.why: Doctors rule out serious problems with a blood test. Police rarely rule out any idea early in a case. The Kremlin did not rule out a link between the attack and President Putin's trip to China.

verbs.correct: To come just before an event
verbs.wrong: To choose the place for an event
verbs.why: Stores get busy in the weeks that lead up to Christmas. Many students feel nervous in the days that lead up to exams. The attack came in the days leading up to a planned meeting in China.

chunks.text: On the night of the bridge attack, Russia struck Kyiv, Ukraine's capital. Zelenskyy said seven [[ballistic missiles]] were fired at two bridges. The strikes {{shut down}} both for a time. Russia said its forces hit military, energy and transport targets. A [[senior]] U.S. defense official {{came out against}} Ukraine's [[long-range]] strikes inside Russia, saying they had not helped end the war. Germany's defense minister {{stood up for}} Ukraine and said strikes on [[military targets]] were legal.

verbs.wrong: To check each car on a road
verbs.why: Heavy snow often shuts down the highway. The city shuts down the main bridge for repairs every spring. The Russian strikes shut down two main bridges in Kyiv for a time.
Many doctors come out against the new health plan. Some mayors come out against higher bridge tolls. An American defense official came out against Ukraine's long-range strikes.

verbs.wrong: To replace someone in a job
verbs.why: Good friends stand up for each other. She always stands up for her younger brother at school. Germany's defense minister stood up for Ukraine.

mainIdea.s: A Ukrainian strike destroyed part of the bridge joining Russia and Crimea, and Russia promised to rebuild it. Road travel stopped, and Russian missiles hit two Kyiv bridges that same night.
mainIdea.why: The attack cut off the road link, and the Kremlin said the bridge would be restored. On the same night, Russian strikes shut down two main bridges in Kyiv.

mainIdea.s: Ukraine hit the Crimea crossing and stopped every car and train from using it. Russian officials called the damage too serious to repair, while all of Ukraine's allies praised the operation.
mainIdea.why: Close, but Russia said trains ran again the same day and the Kremlin said the bridge would be restored. A senior U.S. official also came out against Ukraine's long-range strikes.

mainIdea.s: Engineers in Ukraine finished a new rail line to the southern coast after three years of work. Officials hope this route will lower shipping costs and attract more grain buyers to the region.
mainIdea.why: No new rail line opened. A Ukrainian attack brought down part of the bridge between Russia and Crimea, and Russia attacked bridges in Kyiv.

tf.s: A Ukrainian attack brought down part of the bridge to Crimea.
tf.why: A huge steel arch and a section of road fell into the sea on November 17, 2026.

tf.why: Ukraine's military said the damage cut off the road link and no vehicle could cross.

tf.s: Zelenskyy said his forces spent weeks wearing down Russian air defenses.
tf.why: He said they first knocked out radars, and then came the final strike.

tf.s: The Kremlin ruled out repairing the bridge after the attack.
tf.why: It said the bridge would be restored, so repairs were not ruled out.

tf.s: Russian missiles shut down two main bridges in Kyiv.
tf.why: Zelenskyy said seven ballistic missiles were fired at the two bridges, and both closed for a time.

tf.s: Germany's defense minister came out against Ukraine's strikes in Russia.
tf.why: He stood up for Ukraine and said strikes on military targets were legal. A senior U.S. official was the one who criticized them.

lines.text: Did you see the news about the bridge to Crimea?
I did. A Ukrainian attack {{brought down}} part of it, right?
Yes. A huge arch fell into the sea, and Ukraine's military says the damage {{cut off}} the road link.
Not by road, [[from the looks of it]]. Russia says trains ran again later that day.
It {{went after}} the bridge in 2022 and 2023. The bridge was damaged but {{held up}}.
Zelenskyy says his forces spent weeks {{wearing down}} Russian air defenses. They {{knocked out}} radars first.
The Kremlin says the bridge will be restored. It also didn't {{rule out}} a link to Putin's trip to China.
Right, this came in the days {{leading up to}} his meeting with Trump and Xi. That [[raises the stakes]].
It does. Separately, on the night of the bridge attack, Russian missiles {{shut down}} two main bridges in Kyiv.
[[It doesn't look good]]. Zelenskyy says Ukraine was {{hitting back}}, but the attacks continue on both sides.
Even Ukraine's supporters don't [[see eye to eye]]. A U.S. official {{came out against}} its long-range strikes, and Germany's defense minister {{stood up for}} Ukraine.
Could this be [[a turning point]] in the war?
Nobody can say yet. One expert says crews can {{clean up}} the wreckage fairly quickly, but full road traffic needs more than a year.
